what: Mercury General is an auto and home insurer, writing most of its policies in California, along with smaller books in other states. It sells through independent agents.
customers: California drivers and homeowners, mostly middle-income households.
moat: A large, long-established position in California auto insurance and a low-cost distribution model. California’s strict rate regulation keeps out some competitors.
risks: California regulators must approve rate increases, which delays price rises when costs jump; this caused the $513M loss in 2022.
Wildfires in California, including the January 2025 Los Angeles fires, expose its home book to large losses.
Only one analyst covers the stock.
opportunities: Rate increases have caught up: net income rose from a loss in 2022 to $643M over the last twelve months.
At about 7 times earnings, the shares are cheap if profits hold.
A large investment portfolio earns more as interest rates stay higher.
watch: The combined ratio of its California auto business, and catastrophe losses.
view: Mercury is a California auto and home insurer whose profits depend on two things: how quickly regulators let it raise prices and how often California burns. In 2022 inflation hit before rate increases were approved, and it lost $513 million. Since then prices have caught up and profits have been strong.
At about 7 times earnings the shares are priced for that to end, and the risk is real: a large wildfire can wipe out a year’s profit in the home book. The January 2025 fires showed that exposure.
This turns on catastrophe losses. In a normal year the shares look cheap; in a bad fire year they do not. I would call it a value bet that requires accepting California catastrophe risk.
bull: Rates stay adequate, no major wildfire hits and profits remain high.
bear: A large wildfire or new inflation shock erases profits before regulators approve higher rates.
